text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition Union of Bosnian Social Democrats (UBSD) says it will take part in five-party opposition coalition Joint List in local elections scheduled this summer. It rejects idea of separate party slate.

- Opposition Bosnian Party (BOSS) welcomes decision by European football federation president Lenart Johansson to ban Bosnian teams from European competitions until single Bosnian league is established.

- Independent Union of Bosnian Journalists strongly protests against violent intrusion in editorial offices of Sarajevo-based independent magazine Dani and abuse of its journalists, the Union says in release.

- "All problems of post-Dayton Bosnia are consequences of the fact that neither (Serbian President Slobodan) Milosevic nor (Croatian President Franjo) Tudjman have ever thought of giving up even a small portion of what they have won in war, except what was taken by the International Community in numerous negotiations," the daily says in a commentary.

- $90 million are needed for 10 projects of Bosnia's agricultural reconstruction, Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry says in programme which is to be presented at upcoming doners conference.
- Bosnian state airliner Air Bosnia will fly first commercial flight from Sarajevo to Istanbul on Tuesday, the company says in statement.

- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Forum to hold session on Monday to try to overcome problems such as implementation of cantonal police, municipality borders and creation of Sarajevo city government.
